summary:
PulseBoard is a web-based astronaut health monitoring system designed to support crew health and well-being during space missions. It provides a centralized dashboard to record and monitor important health parameters, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, blood glucose, sleep duration, body weight, and mood.
The system analyzes recorded health readings, generates a wellness score, highlights values that may require attention, and displays health trends over time. It is designed to support astronauts in different mission environments, including spacecraft, space stations, lunar bases, and Mars habitats.
By providing an organized way to monitor physiological changes and maintain health records, PulseBoard aims to improve health awareness, support early identification of potential health concerns, and assist crew members in maintaining their well-being during long-duration space missions.
details:
Project Overview

PulseBoard is a web-based astronaut health monitoring platform developed to support the continuous observation and management of crew health during space missions. Space environments introduce several challenges to human physiology, including microgravity-related cardiovascular changes, sleep disturbances, metabolic changes, and psychological stress. Monitoring these changes is important, particularly during long-duration missions to the Moon and Mars.

Working Principle

The application provides four main sections:

  1. Mission Dashboard: Displays the astronaut's wellness score, health status, and a summary of the latest recorded health parameters.
  2. Vital Signs Monitoring: Allows users to record heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, blood glucose, sleep duration, body weight, mood, and additional symptoms.
  3. Health History: Stores previous health readings, displays historical records, and allows data to be exported in CSV and JSON formats for further analysis.
  4. Crew Profile: Maintains basic crew information and allows the selection of different mission environments, including spacecraft, space stations, lunar bases, and Mars habitats.

Health Assessment and Alerts

PulseBoard evaluates recorded health parameters against predefined reference ranges and generates a wellness score. Values outside the expected ranges are highlighted using normal, warning, and alert indicators. A heart rate trend graph also helps users observe changes across multiple readings.

These features are intended to support health awareness and identify readings that may require further medical attention. The displayed wellness score and reference ranges are educational indicators, not clinically validated astronaut medical assessments.

Technology Used

The project was developed using:

  • HTML5 for the application structure.
  • CSS3 for interface design and responsive layouts.
  • JavaScript for data processing, health assessment, navigation, and interactive functionality.
  • Browser Local Storage for saving health readings and crew profiles.
  • HTML Canvas for visualizing heart rate trends.

Innovation and Impact

The main innovation of PulseBoard is the integration of multiple health parameters, wellness assessment, historical tracking, and mission-specific information into one accessible dashboard.

The system is designed to help astronauts and mission-support personnel organize health information, recognize changes in physiological trends, and support informed health monitoring during space exploration.

Its mission-specific design makes it adaptable to spacecraft, lunar habitats, space stations, and future Mars missions. In the future, the platform could be extended with wearable health sensors, real-time data transmission, predictive analytics, and integration with authorized spaceflight medical systems.

PulseBoard aims to contribute to safer human space exploration by making astronaut health information easier to monitor, understand, and manage.
